thread:
alex: Heads up — I found a reproducible failure mode when applying hotpatches during a staged migration in airgapped clusters. Some components get stuck in "activating" for a long time.

maria: can you paste repro steps?

alex: repro steps:
1) enable staged migration with store-and-forward on
2) push hotpatch bundle that contains a small runtime patch + very large model shard set
3) controller claims bundle activated, operator shows bundle state=Activated, but some component dirs are partially populated and activation health probes fail intermittently

kubectl example for triggering:
```
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: BundleApply
metadata:
  name: hotpatch-2026-03-quick
spec:
  bundleRef: hotpatch-2026-03-quick
  mode: staged
```

jamal: my hunch: activation is gated on manifest/index presence only, not on per-shard completion. sidecar streams shards async; controller sees index and flips activate. activation code then reads components and can hit IO errors.

olivia: I thought we were waiting for manifest checksum verification before activating?
alex: we do verify the manifest, but index presence doesn't mean the heavy shards completed arrival. activation reads component metadata + tries to bind symlinks -> hits partial state.

sara: quick mitigation: activation should write to a temp dir and rename into place once component integrity is verified. atomic move avoids half-baked dirs.

ryan: atomic rename helps on a single filesystem, but streaming sidecar may hold open file descriptors. rename doesn't prove full integrity unless we also verify checksums after final byte.

maria: tradeoff: block activation until every shard verified (slower, safer) vs allow TOP-tier components to go live earlier (quicker to patch security bits).

jamal: what about introducing explicit per-component lifecycle states: FETCHING -> VERIFIED -> READY -> FAILED. Controller requires READY for components in the same activation tier.

olivia: sidecar should own verification: it knows when streaming finished and can compute checksums. sidecar can push aggregated status to the BundleApply status subresource. controller only acts on READY states.

sara: sidecar->controller via status subresource is durable (etcd) so it works in airgapped clusters. downside: chatty writes.

ryan: etcd pressure concern is real for customers with thousands of tiny shards. we should batch status updates and rate-limit them. propose batching window of ~3s and aggregated per-component messages.

maria: propose activation tiers: TOP (critical runtime/security), NORMAL (models, infra), DEFERRED (optional assets). controller may activate if all TOP components are READY even if NORMAL/DEFERRED are still FETCHING.

alex: edge case: partial activation could leave incompatible runtime+model pairs. need a compatibility matrix check before allowing TOP-only activation. if mismatch detected, controller should block or schedule immediate rollback.

jamal: implement short canary window after activation: run health probes + smoke tests; if failures occur in window -> auto-rollback. make window length pluggable per tenant (30s to 10m).

olivia: API impact: keep spec unchanged; extend status only. backward compatible for CLI and operator UX.

ryan: E2E testing: add harness that simulates slow/stalled shard delivery, intermittent IO errors, and file descriptor locks to ensure controller and sidecar cooperate.

maria: telemetry we should add: activation_lag_ms, partial_activation_percent, per-tenant rollback_rate, shard_stream_retries. useful for SLA reports.

sara: operator knobs: max_batched_status_per_second and batched_window_ms to protect etcd and allow customer tuning.

alex: propose implementation steps:
- add per-component tier field + aggregated component state string to BundleApplyStatus
- sidecar emits batched status blobs: [{component, tier, state, checksum}] every batched_window_ms
- controller enforces tiered activation policy, records activation_lag_ms, and triggers canary timers
- add compatibility matrix check and canary auto-rollback path

maria: :thumbsup: sounds good. do a small POC before an RFC so we can size etcd impact.

jamal: I'll take the POC. plan: simulate 1k tiny shards with 10% stalling and measure status writes + controller CPU.

olivia: I'll help with Dedicated testing to verify behavior when model shards are on reserved GPU pools vs local node volumes.

alex: thanks. I'll draft a short RFC with sequence diagrams showing: sidecar streaming -> batched status -> controller reconcile -> tiered activation -> canary window -> rollback. also include operator knobs + telemetry.

sre-bot: New task created: INF-2042 - hotpatch-tiered-activation-poc (assignee: jamal) <https://tracker.redwood.local/browse/INF-2042>

jamal: starting POC this week. will post results and perf numbers in this thread.

ryan: one more thought: consider optional compression/packing for very large model shards in airgapped bundles to reduce transfer time and fewer IO ops. packing trades off space vs decode CPU.

alex: noted. we'll discuss packing as a follow-up RFC. thanks everyone.
